topic.subject: science
topic.title: Crop production and management
topic.scope: kharif and rabi crops, soil preparation, sowing, manure and fertilisers, irrigation, weeding, harvesting, storage

misconceptions.statement: Any crop can grow in any season if we provide enough water.
misconceptions.why: Students often think water is the only limiting factor for plant growth.
misconceptions.fix: Crops like Kharif and Rabi depend on specific temperature, day length, and rainfall patterns, not just water quantity.

probe.question: If we provide plenty of irrigation, can we grow Paddy in the peak of a dry North Indian winter?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because paddy only needs lots of water to grow.

misconceptions.root_belief: one factor determines the outcome of a complex process

misconceptions.statement: Ploughing is done only to kill weeds and has no effect on the soil itself.
misconceptions.why: The removal of weeds is a visible result, while soil aeration is invisible.
misconceptions.fix: Ploughing loosens the soil, allowing roots to breathe easily and penetrate deeper.

probe.question: Why do we turn the soil even if there are no weeds present?
probe.wrong_answer: It is just a traditional habit with no scientific benefit.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: Seeds that float on water are healthy because they are light and easy to sprout.
misconceptions.why: Students may associate lightness with agility or ease of movement.
misconceptions.fix: Healthy seeds are heavy and sink; floating seeds are usually hollow or damaged by pests.

probe.question: You put seeds in a bucket of water and some float. Which ones will you sow?
probe.wrong_answer: The floating ones because they are light.

misconceptions.root_belief: lighter or smaller objects are more active

misconceptions.statement: Fertilizers are the food that plants eat to grow.
misconceptions.why: Students use an analogy with human eating to understand plant nutrition.
misconceptions.fix: Plants make their own food through photosynthesis; fertilizers only provide mineral nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus.

probe.question: What is the primary purpose of adding urea to a field?
probe.wrong_answer: To provide food for the plant to eat.

misconceptions.root_belief: living things must eat external food to grow

misconceptions.statement: Manure is harmful to plants because it is made from animal waste.
misconceptions.why: Everyday associations of 'waste' or 'dung' with germs and disease.
misconceptions.fix: Manure is organic matter that improves soil texture and adds humus, which is very beneficial.

probe.question: Is adding cow dung to soil safe for the crops we eat?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because waste contains toxins that will enter the fruit.

misconceptions.root_belief: waste products are always toxic and harmful

misconceptions.statement: Drip irrigation is less effective because it doesn't soak the whole field.
misconceptions.why: Students believe that 'more water' or 'visible wetness' equals better growth.
misconceptions.fix: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the roots, minimizing wastage and preventing weed growth in empty spaces.

probe.question: Why might a farmer choose drip irrigation over flooding the whole field?
probe.wrong_answer: They wouldn't, because flooding ensures every part of the plant gets water.

misconceptions.root_belief: more of a good thing is always better

misconceptions.statement: Weeds are harmless plants that just happen to grow in the wrong place.
misconceptions.why: Students don't see the invisible competition for resources happening underground.
misconceptions.fix: Weeds actively compete with crops for water, nutrients, space, and light, reducing crop yield.

probe.question: If a few wild grass plants grow among wheat, should the farmer worry?
probe.wrong_answer: No, they are just extra plants and won't affect the wheat.

misconceptions.statement: Grains should be stored while they are slightly moist to keep them fresh.
misconceptions.why: In everyday life, 'fresh' vegetables are often moist or hydrated.
misconceptions.fix: Stored grains must be completely dry to prevent the growth of fungus and bacteria.

probe.question: Why do farmers sun-dry grains before packing them in gunny bags?
probe.wrong_answer: To make them lighter for transport.

misconceptions.root_belief: freshness is always associated with moisture

misconceptions.statement: Paddy and Rice are two completely different species of plants.
misconceptions.why: The change in name after processing (removal of husk) confuses students.
misconceptions.fix: Paddy is the name of the crop in the field; rice is the grain obtained after removing the husk.

probe.question: What is the difference between a paddy field and a rice field?
probe.wrong_answer: They grow different types of grains used for different dishes.

misconceptions.root_belief: different names imply different biological entities

misconceptions.statement: Earthworms are pests because they create holes in the soil.
misconceptions.why: Generalization that any 'worm' found in a farm is a pest that eats crops.
misconceptions.fix: Earthworms are 'friends of the farmer' because they help in loosening soil and adding humus.

probe.question: If you see many earthworms in your field, what should you do?
probe.wrong_answer: Apply pesticides to kill them before they eat the seeds.

misconceptions.root_belief: all small crawling animals are harmful pests

misconceptions.statement: Soil is an inexhaustible source of minerals that never runs out.
misconceptions.why: Soil appears as a massive, permanent part of the earth that doesn't seem to change.
misconceptions.fix: Continuous cultivation of crops makes the soil poor in certain nutrients, requiring replenishment.

probe.question: Why can't we grow the same crop in the same field year after year without adding anything?
probe.wrong_answer: We can, the soil has infinite minerals for plants.

misconceptions.statement: Threshing and Winnowing are the same process.
misconceptions.why: Both involve separating parts of the harvested plant and are done close together in time.
misconceptions.fix: Threshing separates grains from the stalks, while winnowing separates grains from the lighter chaff using wind.

probe.question: Which process specifically requires the help of wind?
probe.wrong_answer: Threshing, because it blows the grain away.

misconceptions.root_belief: related steps in a sequence are identical
